blocks.content: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 gave constitutional status and protection to the Panchayati Raj institutions.

rows: Organize village panchayats as units of self-government
Provide free legal aid and equal opportunity for justice
Secure just and humane work conditions and maternity relief
Separate judiciary from executive in public services

items: Separation of judiciary from the executive under Article 50 was realized in practice through the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act (2002) shifted the scope of Article 45 to early childhood care and converted primary education into a Fundamental Right under Article 21A.
Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 was enacted pursuant to Article 39A to ensure justice is not denied to any citizen due to economic disabilities.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Socio-Economic Measures: The Minimum Wages Act (1948), Maternity Benefit Act (1961), and MGNREGA give practical effect to Directive Principles like Articles 39, 41, and 42.
Grassroots Democracy: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts of 1992 fulfilled Article 40 by giving constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions and Municipalities.
Legal Aid & Justice: Article 39A was operationalized through the Legal Services Authorities Act (1987), establishing NALSA to provide free legal aid.
Separation of Powers: Article 50 was implemented by enacting the Code of Criminal Procedure (1973), separating the judicial function from executive authorities.
Environmental Protection: Article 48A led to key legislations including the Wildlife Protection Act (1972) and the Forest Conservation Act (1980).
